title: Type narrowing and discriminated unions interview drills

items.question: Why use unknown instead of any for fetch().json()?
items.answer: any disables all checking — you can read any property without proof. unknown forces narrowing before use — matches runtime truth that JSON can be anything. Assign to unknown, validate with type guard or Zod, then use typed value. any is for migration only.
items.sixtySeconds: unknown forces narrow. any silences compiler. Guard or Zod at boundary. Never as User after json.

items.question: What is a discriminated union and how do you get exhaustiveness checking?
items.answer: Union of objects sharing literal discriminant — type, kind, status. switch on discriminant narrows each branch. default: const _: never = value — compile error when new variant added without case. satisfies never in TS 4.9+.
followUps: What breaks if discriminant is string not literal?
items.sixtySeconds: Literal tag per variant. switch narrows. never in default for exhaustiveness. Types erase at runtime.

items.question: How do you narrow unknown from Redis GET before using Session type?
items.answer: redis.get returns string | null. If null return null. JSON.parse to unknown not Session. isSession type guard checks userId string and roles string array. If fail delete corrupt key return null. Only then return parsed as Session.
items.sixtySeconds: parse to unknown. guard validates. delete bad cache. null checks. no as Session without guard.

items.question: Difference between type predicate and assertion function?
items.answer: Type predicate x is T returns boolean — use in if (isUser(x)). Assertion function asserts x is T returns void throws — after call compiler knows x is T in rest of block. Assertion for invariants that must hold or crash.
followUps: asserts x is T vs x is T return type?
items.sixtySeconds: Predicate returns boolean if branch. Assertion throws to narrow. assertIsUser after parse.

items.question: Model API success/error as discriminated union — sketch types.
items.answer: type Result<T> = { ok: true; data: T } | { ok: false; error: string; code: number }. switch on ok. true branch has data. false has error. default never for exhaustiveness. Better than throwing for expected HTTP errors.
items.sixtySeconds: ok boolean discriminant. switch exhaustiveness. never default. validate unknown into union at boundary.

items.question: What is wrong with: const user = await res.json() as User?
items.answer: Cast tells compiler to trust without runtime validation. API can return different shape — undefined.email at runtime. Fix: unknown + isUser guard or Zod parse. Code review rejects as at boundaries.
items.sixtySeconds: as is compile-time lie. unknown plus guard. Zod runtime plus inferred type. OpenAPI not runtime proof.
